scientific_integrity: The positive directions are proved by explicit Bezout-parametrized identities whose common divisor is forced to divide \(1\) or \(2\); parity then excludes the latter when necessary. The negative direction is a complete modulo-\(8\) obstruction. Finite computation is used only as regression evidence.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns only the already-characterized special parameters \(d\); it does not classify primitive values for arbitrary \(d\), and it gives no height-asymptotic count of representations.
title: Primitive universality dichotomy for special ternary forms
